Just before WWI, Russia and France held more gold than the rest of the big powers. A thread on Europe's official gold reserves in 1913.

a thread 🧵🗺️
1/ The map (source: IMF, in metric tonnes) puts Russia first with 1,233 tonnes and France second with 1,030. Together they hold more than the next five holders combined.
2/ Germany is third at 438.6 tonnes, then Austria-Hungary at 378.4 and Italy at 355.8. The top five holders account for about 80% of the total shown on the map.
3/ Britain, the centre of global finance, shows only 248 tonnes, less than Italy. The map counts official reserves, and London's role rested on credit and trade, not on a big gold pile.
4/ Small economies hold little: Sweden 41.5, Denmark 31.2, Norway 19.5, Portugal 19.2, Greece 7.2. Spain stands out among the mid-sized states at 140.3.

5/ In 1913 the big powers were all on or near the gold standard, so these tonnes were also the backing for their money. Which figure on the map surprises you? Follow @forummapping for more maps like this.
